assessment: All nine retained PDF pages read and visually inspected, including six figures, Table1, 23 numbered equations, decision/input/set definitions, six footnotes and 28 bibliography entries. Appendix formulas and small map legends were magnified. Printed property/cost functions are independently implemented and unit interfaces checked using clearly labelled analyst fixtures. Original California GIS/network/field inputs, cost-deflation multiplier, author code, underlying citations and external asset availability remain unverified. The original optimiser, hydraulic iteration and fitted EOS are not independently reproduced; this paper is not comprehensively complete.

sections.assessment: Middleton and Bielicki, Energy Policy 37 (2009), 1052–1060; DOI 10.1016/j.enpol.2008.09.049. Received 3 July 2008, accepted 1 September 2008, online 24 December 2008. Abstract describes integrated cost-minimising capacitated network design, with 37 California sources and 14 reservoirs. Copyright preserved.

Read CCS context, infrastructure-scale analogies, seven planning decisions, critiques of direct/straight/nearest-source models and novelty claims. Exact IPCC/MIT/ISGS/Dooley/Kobos and transport originals remain unchecked; pipeline feasibility rhetoric is not a universal exclusion of shipping.

A 1 km US raster combines geographic feature weights. Modified Dijkstra paths are vectorised, overlaps merged and artifacts trimmed. Exact raster, diagonal/edge costs, address corrections and trimming code are missing; preprocessing is not reproduced.

All 14 MILP expressions and variable/input/set definitions read. Continuous capture, transport and injection link to binary openings/diameter choices. CPLEX 11.0 stated. Masses are converted to 25-year lifetime stocks. Incoming-neighbour indexing and outside-set variable definitions need clarification before literal execution.

Read source, compression, pipeline and well cost methods, with footnotes 1–3. Present costs and 11% fixed-charge annualisation; maximum 90% capture, 10 MPa transport/delivery, 75% pump efficiency, 70 USD/MWh and 60 USD/bbl. No joint pressure-drop optimisation or complete capture utility inventory. Radial injectivity determines well count, not layout.

The 37 sources are 21 gas power plants, one coal plant, ten refineries and five cement plants. Fourteen depleted-oil fields are represented by centroids; WestCarb addresses are corrected. Pipeline costs are explicitly artificially deflated. Individual data and the deflation factor are missing.

Read 10/30/50 Mt/year maps, cost/utilisation claims and direct-pipeline cost/length comparisons. Every target is a separate static optimisation. No raw solutions or solver logs retained; maps are demonstrations rather than policy recommendations or annual schedules.

Authors state case results are not generalisable. Future work includes boosters, tax/revenue objectives, staged construction, heuristics and resilience. All infrastructure is currently simultaneous. ZERT support during Los Alamos 2006–07; Michael Kuby acknowledged.

Read Eqs15–23, all signs/powers, radial Darcy derivation and footnotes 5–6 in magnified renders. Pressure and viscosity interfaces are checked separately from unknown author implementation. Printed property/well-cost functions are independently evaluated; no field calibration follows.

All 28 bibliography entries read; Dooley2006 continues from p8 to p9. Every direct entry is mapped below, including Stephens2005. Their originals remain unverified. A later local EOS calculation does not verify the cited article or this regression.

Variables a/b are defined only on source/reservoir sets elsewhere, so zero extension also needs specification. Preserve the source notation; no silent correction or unpublished-code failure claim.
Capture requires an open source and is bounded by its lifetime maximum. Partial capture allowed; 90% maximum stated but individual input basis missing.
Injection requires an open reservoir and lifetime stock capacity. This is not a year-specific pressure-limited rate.
Total capture is at least T. Equality to storage requires clarified lossless conservation. No net-GHG objective or annual schedule.
At most one diameter per directed candidate arc. Arc directions/data and construction stages are not supplied.
Binary pipeline/diameter selection. Tonnes remain continuous; neighbour quantifiers need a concrete graph.
Binary source opening; fixed infrastructure cost differs from marginal capture.
Binary reservoir opening, not an integer well-layout decision.
Nonnegative directional lifetime flow. Reverse-arc handling requires original graph data.
Printed j∈S quantifier differs from a_i index; preserved pending clarification. Intended nonnegative capture is clear, but literal indexing is not silently repaired.
Nonnegative stored lifetime mass. No stock evolution, outages or retained-carbon horizon.
Mass kg/s, density kg/m3 and ΔP MPa numerically give MW after unit conversions cancel. Efficiency 0.75 stated. This pump approximation is not a complete capture/compressor utility inventory.

Darcy–Weisbach with v=4m_dot/(rho pi D²), L km and D m gives the printed numerical expression in Pa. Eq15 labels ΔP MPa. An explicit 1e6 conversion is required at that interface. Raw literal and SI-expressed MPa diagnostics stay separate; author code is unavailable.

ln(r1/r2)≈7.5, h m, k m2, rho kg/m3, mu MPa·s and pressures MPa give kg/s. Eq20 mPa·s requires multiplication by 1e-9. Steady radial Darcy flow does not model pressure-front evolution, relative permeability or interference.

With density kg/m3, g=9.81 m/s² and depth km, the expression gives Pa. MPa interfaces need conversion. Main p4 refers to head Eq19, while the actual head equation is18. Density is treated as constant.

ΔT=T−340 K and ΔP=P−25 MPa. All ten coefficients/signs/powers magnified and implemented. The fit data, error and validity interval are missing; nine analyst evaluations are not independent EOS validation.

Output mPa·s, explicitly distinguished from Eq17 MPa·s in footnote6. At the origin, 0.06370 mPa·s =6.37e-11 MPa·s. All terms implemented; correlation validity over an unstated domain is not established.
Depth d inherits km from Eq18; coefficients depend on these units. Evaluations at analyst depths 1/2/3 km are function checks, not original field costs or harmonised current USD.
Depth km, source USD basis. Function evaluation is not a complete well CAPEX/OPEX inventory.
Oil price 60 USD/bbl stated; depth km. No field depths or original well-count/pressure iteration supplied.

equations.check: Footnote5 integrates radial Darcy velocity and area 2pi rh to a logarithmic factor. Printed integration limits versus positive ln(r1/r2) need an explicit signed-flow convention. No transient or multiphase derivation is supplied.

variables: Nodes i/j, neighbour sets Ni/Nj, source set S, reservoir set R and discrete diameter set D. Eq4 incoming indexing and outside-set a/b treatment unresolved.
a_i capture, x_ij transported and b_j stored: lifetime tonnes over 25 years. Capacities Qs/Qp/Qr must share that basis; source kt/year and reservoir stock kt are distinct.
Binary s_i/r_j openings and y_ijd diameter choices. Well count is estimated outside this network MILP; no optimised well layout is supplied.
F coefficients: fixed present USD. V coefficients: present-valued USD/t. Annual outputs use an 11% fixed-charge factor. Exact cost arrays and source-specific financing conversions missing.
T in Eq7 means mass target; T in Eq19 means temperature K. Annualised result targets do not introduce per-year decision variables.
Friction f=0.015, diameter m, length km, mass flow kg/s and density kg/m3. Eq16 gives Pa; Eq15 specifies MPa.

Pump efficiency 0.75, electricity 70 USD/MWh, oil 60 USD/bbl and transport/delivery pressure 10 MPa. Pressure basis and thermal phase conditions incompletely specified; pressure above critical alone does not determine phase.
Radial k m2, h m, log-radius ratio≈7.5, injection/far-field MPa and viscosity MPa·s. Eq20 gives mPa·s; conversion factor 1e-9 is expressly required by footnote6.
Depth d km in head/well costs differs from diameter index d∈D. Gravity 9.81 m/s²; head expression outputs Pa.
Fit origin 340 K/25 MPa. Density kg/m3 and viscosity mPa·s. Fit domain/data, mixture behaviour and errors are not supplied.
1 km raster uses orthogonal/diagonal cell centres; feature weights add. Original raster, edge costs and trimming are missing.
Corrected WestCarb2008 selection: 37 sources/14 oil fields. Maximum 90% capture. The Table1 mean and roughly 56 Mt/year maximum need original input definitions.
All infrastructure is simultaneous; a 25-year conversion horizon does not specify readiness, operating calendars or pressure evolution.
Pipeline cost deflation is disclosed without its factor. Demonstration curves cannot supply calibrated actual prices or utility/GHG inventories.

claims.assessment: Historical context; exact cited originals remain unverified. No current policy or universal pipeline-only conclusion inferred.

claims.claim: Geographic candidate networks improve direct/straight/nearest matching.
claims.assessment: Method description supports the capability. Raster and modified algorithm missing; novelty comparisons need the prior originals.

claims.claim: MILP jointly chooses sources, sinks, flow and pipe sizes to minimise costs.
claims.assessment: Objective, binary domains and capacity links support this. Eq4 notation and case arrays remain unresolved; no annual dynamic pressure model.

claims.claim: Injectivity estimates well numbers from properties and P/T.
claims.assessment: Well count is estimated, layout is not optimised. Pressure boosters, joint hydraulics and temporal deployment remain extensions.

claims.claim: 10 Mt/year: 258 km, five sources, two reservoirs and 41.71 USD/t.
claims.assessment: Attributed result inspected. No original route/cost matrix or deflation factor; not independently reproduced or an actual-price benchmark.

claims.claim: 30 Mt/year: 18 sources/eight reservoirs/43.27 USD/t; 50 Mt/year: 33 sources/12 reservoirs/24-inch trunk.
claims.assessment: Author solutions read. Distinct optimisations, not a staged buildout. No raw solutions or solver certificate retained.

claims.claim: Above 100 kt/year, mean source utilisation 99% and reservoir utilisation 3.1%.
claims.assessment: Averaging population and stock/rate denominators are missing. Preserved as reported, not independently reconstructed.

claims.claim: Capture 35–55 USD/t, storage 1.50–5.50 USD/t and transport usually below 1 USD/t.
claims.assessment: Reported case prices; pipeline costs also explicitly deflated. No general cost calibration or complete capture utility inventory.

claims.claim: Direct pipelines cannot beat networked solutions because paths are nested.
claims.assessment: Feasible-set dominance is conditional on identical costs/constraints and exact solutions. Case arrays are missing; no quantified independent rerun.

claims.claim: Dedicated pipelines typically cost 80% more, maximum 105%; total cost rises ~1.5%, with 48M USD at 54 Mt/year.
claims.assessment: Reported comparisons, based on network costs as denominator. This is not an 80% reduction from the dedicated base or a GHG credit.

claims.claim: Dedicated length exceeds 7,000 km at 56 Mt/year and is more than triple the network.
claims.assessment: Prose and plotted pattern read. No precise curve digitisation or independent routing; targets are not cumulative construction.

claims.claim: Staging, tax/revenue objectives and resilience are possible extensions.
claims.assessment: Identified future work; the 2009 case does not demonstrate annual readiness, failure resilience or time-dependent reservoir response.
